beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:hushed, intrigued]About seven thousand years ago, herders in Arabia built giant stone ^rectangles. [act:building, a little amazed]Not a few: more than sixteen ^hundred of them.
[d:tension][act:the strange detail, leaning in][tune:fall]Then they filled them with cattle ^horns.

[d:calm][act:plain, orienting]They are scattered across the north-west of the peninsula, around ^AlUla. [act:explaining, plain]Archaeologists call them ^mustatils, from the Arabic word for ^rectangle.

[d:build][go:2|0][act:quietly amazed]They were first spotted from ^above, in satellite ^images. [act:a light smile]From the air, the long outlines looked a little like farm gates laid flat, so they were nicknamed ^gates. [p:0.93][act:steady, giving a sense of scale]And some are more than half a ^kilometre long: about five football pitches, end to ^end.

[d:build][act:precise, building]At one end of each rectangle sits a raised ^head: a small chamber, about the size of a bedroom, and standing ^stones. [act:vivid, careful]In one near AlUla, excavators counted the pieces they found ^inside. [p:0.9][act:the number, slowly]Two hundred and forty-seven fragments of skulls and ^horns. [act:plain][tune:fall]Mostly ^cattle.

[d:build][act:curious, the method][tune:rise]So how old are ^they? [act:explaining, clear]Bone and charcoal were once alive, and they hold a little radioactive ^carbon that fades after death at a steady pace, like sand running through an ^hourglass. [act:the key idea]Measure what's left, and you know when it ^died. [p:0.93][act:the reveal, strong]Here, the dates fall in the {6th|sixth} millennium ^BCE, more than seven thousand years ago. [act:context, wonder]Some two thousand years before the first phase of ^Stonehenge.
[d:aside][act:practical, light]And they weren't giant building ^sites. [p:0.93][act:explaining, plain]Ten people could raise one in a few ^weeks.

[d:reveal][act:fair, weighing][tune:rise]So what were they ^for? [act:presenting it, fair]The excavators see a ^cattle cult: horns and skulls laid in the chamber, and people gathering from far ^away. [act:the counterpoint, fair]Other teams read@present them as ^markers, claiming land along herding ^routes, like flags pinned on a ^map.

[d:build][act:a telling detail, gentle]And none is much grander than the ^others. [p:0.93][act:explaining, thoughtful]No giant one, built by a ruler to show his ^power. [act:thoughtful][tune:fall]Builders without ^kings, perhaps.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm authority][tune:rise]Monuments older than Stonehenge, in the Arabian ^desert@noun? [act:the verdict, even][tune:fall]*Strong ^evidence*. [act:fair, clear]The digs and the dates are ^solid. [act:honest, open]What the rectangles ^meant is still being ^weighed.

[d:tension][p:0.93][act:explaining, curious]A tooth keeps a chemical trace of the water and plants an animal grew up on, a little like a ^passport stamp. [act:the last word, warm][tune:fall]So the cattle's teeth may yet tell us where the herds came ^from.
